chunks: Humeyd ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Abdullah ibn Wazzah from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who passed away and left her husband, and her mother, and her father. He said: 'It is from six shares – for the husband is the half, being three shares, and for the mother is the one-third, being two shares, and for the father is the one-sixth, being one share'.
ai.seo_question: How is the estate divided when a woman dies leaving her husband, mother, and father?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific fractional shares (fara'id) for a deceased woman's husband, mother, and father, illustrating the application of Quranic inheritance rules in the presence of multiple heirs. It highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of how the mother's share is fixed at one-third when there are no siblings or descendants, while the father receives a one-sixth share as a Quranic heir rather than a residuary in this specific configuration. This case serves as a foundational example in fiqh for calculating estates where the mother and father both inherit simultaneously alongside the spouse.
